newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open mixed.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open mixed.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were seen opening mixed on Wednesday.

Gold was weaker in London, as the dollar held its ground against the mark and the yen, deflecting interest away from precious metals markets overseas. Platinum and palladium were hammered by massive liquidation overnight on TOCOM, which took prices limit down.
COMEX December gold was seen opening unchanged to up $1.00 an ounce from Wednesday's close of $322.50, after trading a $322.10-$323.50 range in overnight ACCESS trade.
COMEX gold stocks were unchanged Wednesday at 944,791 ounces, while COMEX silver stocks rose 5,062 ounces to 169,681,448, after hitting eight-months lows earlier this week.
COMEX September silver was seen opening unchanged to 2.00 cents lower from Wednesday's close at $4.333 an ounce.
NYMEX October platinum was expected to open down $3.00 to $7.00 an ounce from the previous close at $431.60.
NYMEX September palladium was seen opening down $3.00 to $7.00 an ounce also from the previous close at $215.60.
TOCOM platinum group metals (PGMs) went limit down overnight on fund liquidation, following heavy producer selling in the previous selling.
